text:
I need an email to win back customers who cancelled. I own a home cleaning company with 18 cleaners.

What's true:
- We have 212 regular customers. 64 cancelled in the last year. In exit surveys, the most common reason was price, then a different cleaner showing up each time.
- An every-other-week cleaning for a 3-bedroom house costs $165 with us. The app services in our area charge about $140.
- Our cleaners are employees, not contractors. We pay $21 an hour and carry insurance on every visit.
- Last year 7 of our 18 cleaners left, so about 4 in 10 customers had their regular cleaner change at least once.
- We now give each customer a regular cleaner and a named backup.
- Returning customers get their first cleaning for $99.

I want the email to promise that you'll get the same cleaner every single time. Keep it to about 150 words.

I didn't promise "the same cleaner every single time." Your setup is a regular cleaner plus a named backup, so the backup will sometimes come. Last year 7 of your 18 cleaners left, so cleaners will change again. The people you're emailing left partly because of that. If you promise "every time" and break it, you'll likely lose them for good. The email promises what you can actually keep.

<final_document>
**Subject:** We listened. Come back for $99.

Hi [First Name],

When you left [Company], you told us why. The price was one reason. The other was seeing a different cleaner at your door too often. We heard you.

Here's what's changed. Every customer now has one regular cleaner who gets to know your home. You also get a named backup, so if your cleaner is sick or on vacation, you'll know who's coming instead.

About price: yes, the app services charge less. Here's what the difference pays for. Our cleaners are employees, not gig contractors. We pay them $21 an hour, and every visit is fully insured. If anything goes wrong, you deal with us directly.

We'd love to show you the difference. As a returning customer, your first cleaning is $99.

[Book your cleaning] or just reply to this email.

Thanks,
[Your Name]
Owner, [Company]
</final_document>

A few notes:
- If you'd rather show the price gap in numbers, you could add "about $25 less for a typical 3-bedroom." Being upfront about the cost tends to build trust with people who already know your prices.
- If you have a stat on how long cleaners now stay, or how often the backup actually comes, it would back up the claim better than a promise.
